records.title: The Cursed Ruins of Bhangarh Fort
records.summary: Constructed in the 16th century in the Alwar district of Rajasthan, the deserted city of Bhangarh is famously known as the most haunted historical monument in India. According to circulating folklore, a dark sorcerer named Guru Balu Nath cursed the citadel after shadows of royal mansions touched his forbidden sanctuary, or alternatively, a lovelorn tantric cursed the city with eternal damnation after being crushed by a boulder. The Archaeological Survey of India has famously posted warning signboards barring public entry between sunset and sunrise.
records.historical_period: Modern Urban Folklore (originating 17th Century, circulating post-1970)

records.title: The Whispering Banyan of Sanjay Van
records.summary: Spanning over 700 acres near Qutub Minar in South Delhi, Sanjay Van is a sprawling wilderness preserve crisscrossed with medieval Sufi mausoleums and overgrown ancient fortifications. Urban legend claims that nocturnal visitors frequently encounter a woman in white robes drifting among the branches of aged banyan trees, who abruptly vanishes when approached. Others report the disembodied sound of crying infants and sudden temperature drops near the old stone graves, making it one of the capital's prominent supernatural walking routes.
alternate_names: The White Ghost of Sanjay Van

records.title: The Black Sand Whispers of Dumas Beach
records.summary: Located along the Arabian Sea near Surat in Gujarat, Dumas Beach is famed for its stark black sands, which local lore attributes to centuries of historical use as a Hindu cremation site. The urban legend warns that negative spiritual energies remain bound to the shoreline. Strollers walking the strand alone after midnight report hearing hushed whispers, spectral footsteps echoing on the sand behind them, and dogs howling persistently at empty stretches of surf, with several circulating accounts of solitary walkers wandering into the waves.

records.title: The White Lady of the Delhi Ridge
records.summary: Extending across northern Delhi, the rugged Ridge forest holds memories of the 1857 siege of Delhi and forgotten colonial skirmishes. A widely circulated motorist legend claims that late-night drivers along Cantonment Road and the Flagstaff Tower stretch encounter an elegant lady clad in white seeking a ride. Drivers who accelerate past the phantom frequently report glimpsing her sprinting effortlessly alongside their moving car window, maintaining equal velocity before vanishing into the thorn scrub.

records.title: The Phantom Officers of GP Block Meerut
records.summary: In the historic cantonment city of Meerut in Uttar Pradesh, a decrepit double-storey colonial bungalow known as GP Block has stood abandoned for decades behind overgrown foliage. Urban legend asserts that witnesses passing the compound at night have observed four phantom men seated around a rooftop table illuminated by candlelight, drinking and conversing silently. Other accounts describe a woman in red robes emerging from the vacant doorway, causing locals to steer clear of the property after dark.

records.title: Kuldhara: The Deserted Cursed Village
records.summary: Situated fifteen kilometres west of Jaisalmer in the Thar Desert, the ruins of Kuldhara stand preserved under desolate skies. Once a prosperous settlement of Paliwal Brahmins founded in the 13th century, the entire population of eighty-four adjoining villages evacuated en masse overnight in 1825 to protect a maiden from the predatory desires of an oppressive prime minister, Salim Singh. Before departing forever, the elders uttered a generational curse forbidding anyone from ever reinhabiting the village, leaving its sandstone roofs to collapse into enduring silence.
records.historical_period: Early 19th Century (evacuated 1825, urban legend sustained present)

records.title: The Malabar Hill Phantom
records.summary: Perched above the Arabian Sea in South Mumbai, Malabar Hill is renowned for ancient temples, sacred tanks, and lush colonial tree canopies. A long-standing urban legend among Mumbai night commuters concerns a spectral figure said to walk the quiet lanes between Banganga Tank and the Hanging Gardens. Late-night pedestrians have reported encountering a solitary man in antiquated Parsi attire who glides without sound and dissolves as morning sea mist rolls across the hill.

records.title: The Headless Boy of Kurseong Dow Hill
records.summary: Set amidst dense pine and oak forests in the Darjeeling Himalayan hills, the town of Kurseong houses the historic Victoria Boys' School, built during British colonial rule. Along a secluded woodland trail known locally as the 'Death Road' connecting the school to Dow Hill forest, woodcutters and students have repeatedly reported sightings of a headless adolescent boy who wanders along the misty trail and vanishes abruptly into thick underbrush, accompanied by uncanny sensations of being watched.
records.historical_period: Post-Colonial Era to Present (circulating actively since 1960s)

records.title: The Reincarnation Case of Shanti Devi
records.summary: Born in Delhi in 1926, young Shanti Devi began speaking of her past life in Mathura at age four, calling herself Lugdi and describing in granular detail her former husband, home architecture, and fatal childbirth in 1925. In 1935, a national inquiry committee formed by Mahatma Gandhi escorted her to Mathura, where she accurately identified her previous home, relatives, and secret storage chambers without prior visitation. The case became a worldwide benchmark in twentieth-century parapsychological and urban folklore investigations.
records.region_or_community: Old Delhi and Mathura, Uttar Pradesh

records.title: The Calling Waters of Agrasen ki Baoli
records.summary: Hidden in the urban core of New Delhi near Connaught Place, Agrasen ki Baoli is a 60-metre-long 14th-century stepwell featuring 108 stone steps plunging into the earth. Circulating contemporary urban folklore alleges that before the well dried out, the stagnant black waters possessed hypnotic powers, whispering invitations that induced visitors to leap into its depths. Modern visitors continue to report feelings of intense dread and auditory illusions when descending alone into its lowest shadowed stone alcoves.
records.historical_period: Medieval origin (Tughlaq/Lodi era), Urban legend active late 20th century
